statement: For 2D rectangular knapsack with 8-12 item types, SA over joint (ordering × per-item-heuristic) space achieves ~95.2/100, a 0.37-point improvement over ordering-only hill-climbing. The per-item heuristic dimension is the key lever; SA over orderings alone matches hill-climbing.
regime: M=8-12 item types, bins 900-2000, 1s time budget, 4 MaxRects heuristics (BSSF/BAF/BL/BLSF)
mechanism: Hill-climbing exhausts the ordering space for M=8-12 (O(M²) neighborhood is small enough). The actual unexplored dimension is per-item heuristic assignment: which placement heuristic to use for each item type. SA over the joint space of orderings and per-item heuristic assignments finds combinations where different items benefit from different heuristics — e.g., large items placed with bottom-left while small items use best-short-side-fit.
applicability_bounds: Holds for M=8-12 with 4 heuristics. For larger M, ordering search may regain importance. For more heuristics, the per-item heuristic dimension grows combinatorially.

statement: Residual gap filling after ordered packing provides zero additional value when per-item heuristic selection is optimized. The ordered pack with individually-tuned heuristics per item type leaves no exploitable residual space.
regime: M=8-12 item types, bins 900-2000, MaxRects with 4 heuristics, SA-optimized per-item heuristic assignment
mechanism: Gap filling tries to place remaining copies of item types (sorted by value density) into free rectangles left after ordered packing. When per-item heuristic selection is optimized, the packing already achieves near-maximal space utilization, leaving free rectangles too small for any item type.
applicability_bounds: May not hold if per-item heuristic selection is NOT optimized (i.e., with fixed heuristic, gap filling might contribute). Also may not hold for very large bins where more residual space exists.
